name: CapCut Split-Mask Gradient Type
use_when: A clean title, caption-like title, or minimal text card needs a subtle premium gradient or shadowed edge.
The base word is large enough for a top/bottom tone change to remain visible and readable.
The editor wants polish without adding heavy glow, shadow, or motion.
avoid_when: The text is small, dense, or accessibility-critical.
The background is too complex for a subtle gradient to preserve contrast.
The gradient makes the text edge softer or slower to read than a flat color.
The effect is being used only to make basic typography look expensive.

timeline_pattern.pattern: base_background_or_footage -> base_text -> duplicate_lighter_text -> compound_top_text -> Split_mask -> feather_mask -> position_gradient_boundary -> phone_size_qc
timeline_pattern.duplicate_rule: The duplicate text must match the base text exactly before the gradient mask is applied.
timeline_pattern.mask_rule: Use the split mask and feather to reveal only part of the lighter text layer.
timeline_pattern.boundary_rule: Move the mask boundary until the gradient supports the word shape rather than hiding it.

motion.rule: This is usually a static polish layer; add motion only if the gradient reveal has a clear story or beat job.

keyframe_values.feather: A Split mask feather around 35 can be a clean starting point for large title text.
keyframe_values.top_color: Use a slightly lighter or metallic-gray duplicate when the base text is dark.
keyframe_values.placement: Pull the split-mask line down for a subtle lower shadow or up for a brighter upper highlight, then review at delivery size.

sound.rule: No SFX is required for a static gradient type treatment.

captions.rule: Do not apply this treatment to continuous captions unless readability remains stronger than a plain caption style.

color.rule: Gradient polish is approved only when the base and duplicate colors keep crisp edge contrast on the actual background.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use duplicate drawtext/pre-rendered text layers with a generated grayscale gradient alpha mask and alphamerge, or use maskedmerge for direct two-color blending when no reusable alpha foreground is needed; compare contact frames against a flat text fallback.
implementation.remotion: Use layered text with a CSS mask-image, SVG mask, clipped gradient overlay, or CSS gradient fill, storing baseColor, topColor, maskMode, maskFeather, mask bounds, and contrastQcStatus.
implementation.blender: Use text material gradients or duplicate text objects with a soft alpha mask in the compositor.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Create base text, duplicate it, make the top copy slightly lighter, compound the top text, add Video > Mask > Split, increase Feather around 35, and move the mask line until the gradient or subtle shadow feels clean.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Duplicate Essential Graphics text, recolor the upper layer, apply a feathered mask or track matte, and test readability against a flat version.

common_mistakes: Applying the gradient to small captions where it reduces accessibility.
Misaligning duplicate text layers before compounding.
Using too much feather until the word looks blurry.
Choosing metallic or low-contrast colors that disappear on mobile.
Adding gradient polish before fixing font, spacing, and line breaks.
qc: Does the gradient version read as clearly as or better than flat text?
Are duplicate text layers perfectly aligned?
Does feathering avoid blurry or muddy edges?
Does the treatment survive phone-size preview on bright and dark frames?
Is the effect limited to large title or emphasis text rather than dense subtitles?
Is the mask mode intentional, with no unexpected alpha/luminance reversal?
